models.title: Heltec HT-HC33 Waterproof Case
models.description: A waterproof case for the Heltec HT-HC33 (ESP32-S3 Wi-Fi HaLow board) and one 18650, in three stacked pieces. At the bottom, the battery case holds the cell between two contact plates, with a channel carrying the far lead back; it wraps the cell in a 45° teardrop that carries its sealing flange, so nothing needs supports. On it, the MCU plate carries the board on pinned standoffs, with a hole under the board's battery socket for the lead. On top, the cover: the SMA bulkhead for a 915 MHz antenna comes straight out of one end face, its inner nut locked in a hex pocket deep in the wall, and the USB-C comes out of the other end face behind a hinged door. The door carries a plug that pushes into the USB opening: a TPU sleeve, slightly oversize, whose ribs pop into matching grooves in the opening's walls, so the seal presses on the opening, not the hinge, and the ribs hold it shut. The hinge pin is a filament offcut. Both joints between the pieces seal on TPU 75A printed in place, and a TPU washer is printed into the panel under the SMA's inner nut. Ten M3 × 16 cap screws run straight down the middle of the seal, three along each side and two in each end: heads up in the battery case's flange, through both seals and into bare pilots in the cover. Round each one the TPU widens to a pad the screw threads through, and the cover's ridge widens to a disc that presses it. 84 × 48 × 38 mm. Not yet test-printed.

models.title: Under-Desk Cord Protector
models.description: Modular cord cradle that screws to the underside of a desk. Each 150 mm segment interlocks with the next through a rib-and-groove joint that follows the whole profile — print as many as your desk is wide. models.title: Kobo Clara HD MeshCore Grip
models.description: A sealed handheld grip that turns a Kobo Clara HD into a MeshCore device without modifying it. The Kobo, held in landscape, slides its chin (the wide bezel at its bottom edge) sideways into a slot in the grip, onto a 90° micro USB plug that charges it, and a soft TPU pad in the slot's floor holds it. In front of the chin a 2.13" e-paper stands under a screwed-on bezel. The grip is an 18650 cylinder, flush with the front and standing out at the back, whose depth carries on inward behind the Kobo; its edges are rounded and finger indents run up both sides. Inside: the cell; a TP4056 USB-C charger above it, its port through the right side under the first antenna; three Seeed XIAO boards (an nRF and two SX1262 radios) held by zip ties; and two SMA bulkheads in the top. Sealed by the dry-bag node's rules: PCTG body and lids, soft TPU seals squeezed from the side, screws outside the seals. The back cover's tongue presses into a U-section TPU 85A gasket in a groove round the grip's back rim, with twenty M3 screws in a lane round the whole edge outside it, every corner and about every 20 mm; a smooth boss lifts the seal over the second SMA. A TPU 70A frame seals the bezel to the panel, the SMAs seal on TPU washers, the USB-C takes a TPU plug, and the micro USB plug and the display's wires are potted where they pass in. 80 × 125 × 30.3 mm. Kobo dimensions are Kobo's spec; the screen, button, USB and display positions are estimates. Not yet printed.

models.title: Meshtastic Dry-Bag Node
models.description: A Meshtastic/MeshCore node in a sealed box that winches itself up into a tree. You throw a line over a branch or two and tie both ends to the node's two reels; each reel winds its end in, and the node climbs the line with no tie line left hanging. The box sits in the middle, a reel either side, each reel holding 150–200 ft of 1/8" Dacron, the line's end wedged into a V jam cleat in the drum's core. Each reel turns between two big flat skeleton plates of PCTG, each inside 220 × 220 mm: a ring round the reel with spokes, members from the ring and the roller window back to the plate's inner edge, four dovetailed crossmembers round the reel, and a window of four rollers on top of its outer edge that holds the line both ways. Each reel turns in two big print-in-place roller bearings pressed into its plates, on a journal at the front and its hub at the back. Each roller is a printed sleeve with a print-in-place roller bearing pressed into each end. Each plate's inner edge sits in a little channel on the box's side, indexed by two square blocks, and bolted at 45°. The box is TPU 64D with a solid back wall, and opens at the front. The motors stand on the back wall inside, their pinions' hubs out through TPU lip seals; behind it, under a small bolt-on cover each side, each pinion drives two herringbone idlers, on print-in-place roller bearings in their hubs, onto an output gear on the reel's axis, whose hub runs out through a lip seal in the box's back slab into the reel's hub. The gears are module 2.25 and 16 mm wide, sized up so the printed parts run at low stress. The front door carries the protection board, the winch XIAO nRF52840 Sense, two DRV8871 drivers and the 12 V boost, and the saddles that hold the 32140 LiFePO4 cell standing up. The radio kit sits on the right wall under the N bulkhead in the top, within its 6" pigtail, with room for a 1 W module instead; the antenna's stem is part of the box. The solar panel hangs under the front at 45°, facing forward and up, its edges in two grooved bars through a spine screwed up into the floor. The front door seals on a tongue wider than the groove round the TPU rim, with M5 × 10 screws outside the seal threading 8 mm into the TPU. All holes are round, no supports anywhere. Box 98 × 136 × 186 mm, 264 mm across its back slab. Not yet test-printed.

models.title: Spool Roller Stand (Dry Box)
models.description: A filament spool roller stand for a 300 × 200 × 240 mm dry box interior, sized around the Bambu Lab 200 mm spool — four lanes wide to fill the box, or a single lane on its own. Every lane runs its own pair of rollers on its own pegs, so every spool unwinds independently. The walls between lanes do the supporting: a 608 presses into each end of a roller, one peg through a wall carries both neighbouring rollers at once, and a 0.5 mm shoulder on the peg holds each roller off the flat wall — no pockets, so the walls print flat with nothing to bridge. Each roller flange tapers at 40° from the wall face down to the running surface, filling the 2 mm between spool and wall, so a spool dropped in has one place to go and no edge to perch on. The roller spacing is solved rather than chosen — asking for the spool to sit 8 mm off the floor is what puts the rollers 156.4 mm apart, with the rims meeting them 42.8° off vertical. Filament leaves the bottom of a spool into a PTFE tube whose mouth is held by a clip just behind the spool, clear of it; the tube runs flat through loops in a round-bottomed groove sunk half the tile's thickness, under the back roller to a second clip tucked behind it, and leaves the tile there for a push-fit bulkhead; a drilling template marks a bulkhead hole at each lane centre, and a second marks the tiles' screw-down holes on the box floor. The floor splits into one dovetailed tile per lane, and the walls split into a left, a centre and a right the same way, so every part fits a 220 mm bed; the four-lane templates print in dovetailed halves, the one-lane ones whole. Screw pads through the lattice let the stand be fixed down, and each wall is one crescent-shaped piece — tall at the back, low through the middle, up again at the front. Walls sit on the floor on full-length V ridges, and are screwed down by three M3s up through the floor — front, middle and back — with the two tiles under a centre wall lapping at each. One hex beam per lane, nested end to end, runs through the top back of the walls, clear of the seated spools, and an M3 screw through the back of each wall locks the wall and both beam ends in it together. Spool size, ride height, lane count, roller and bearing dimensions, the PTFE run and the box are all adjustable.

models.title: Spool Dry Box Module
models.description: A sealed dry box for one 200 mm spool, printed in pieces on a Snapmaker U1 with 75A TPU gaskets printed in place. Two round side walls, the spool's diameter plus 2 mm clearance and 3 mm wall each side, with curved 3 mm panels between them. The spool sits on two rollers, as on the filament spool roller, each in an ear that bulges out of the bottom of both walls with its axle moulded into them and an ear plate closing it round. The lid is the top and front half, cut off on a diagonal plane through the axis from just past the front roller to the back: both walls' tops, a third roller in an ear at the top that rests on the spool, and the panels between. It hinges at the back on an M3 and an over-centre draw latch pulls it shut at the front. The cut is sealed like every other joint, with no screws: a ridge on the lid presses into a TPU bead in a groove round the base's side, and the walls carry a lip inward along the cut wide enough for it. Every panel edge flares out to a ridge that presses into a TPU bead in a groove on a rib round the inside of each wall, and M3 cap screws run through the wall, straight down the middle of the TPU channel, into a boss in the panel's edge. Where a panel meets an ear plate, a TPU strip printed into its end presses on it. Work in progress: the top roller has no spring yet, and the walls and panels are 3 mm.

models.title: Duct Airflow Modules (100 mm)
models.description: A kit of airflow modules for 100 mm (4") dryer duct — for pulling exhaust and a slight vacuum from printer enclosures and choosing which run the fan draws on — that all join the same way. Every module has a socket at one end and a plug at the other. The plug pushes in, turns 20° to lock, and the lugs ride a ramp that pulls it in half a millimetre onto a TPU 75A liner printed into the socket's floor. A printed key drops into two notches that only line up once it has turned home, so it can't turn back; eight M3 cap-screw spots round each joint can clamp it harder, into self-tapped pilots or nuts. The modules are straight tubes, 45° elbows (two make a 90° bend), duct spigots on a socket or a plug, a socket coupler, servo butterfly valves, and two kinds of manifold. A polar manifold is a hub with a trunk and branches leaning out 45° round it. A cubic manifold is unit cubes laid out cell by cell, with a plug or socket on any face you name, each cell twisting onto the one before it. There are also sensor sections: a sealed cap that holds a cheap breakout board (BME280, SHT31, AHT20, SGP30/40, ENS160 and others) against a window into the duct, and a venturi with pressure taps for a differential pressure sensor to measure the flow. Every part prints in PETG without supports, nothing overhangs past 45°, and the TPU prints in place on a multi-material printer. The butterfly valves are turned by an SG90 on the disc's axis. The original bolt flange is still an option for the hub, valve and duct spigot.

filament.note: Every rigid part. PETG keeps its shape in warm enclosure exhaust where PLA creeps.

models.title: Telescoping Antenna Mast
models.description: A print-in-place telescoping mast for a small 915 MHz antenna. Five thin round tubes print nested in one 250 mm-tall piece (sized for a Qidi Q2) and reach 1.1 m. To raise a section, pull it to its stop, twist it 60° and let go: three lugs drop into dips in the teeth below and hold its weight. To lower it, lift, twist back and push down. The outer tube's foot and the inner tube's top are 45° threads, so two prints and a coupler make a 2.2 m mast.

models.title: Lattice Antenna Mast
models.description: A 20 ft guyed antenna mast for a solar mesh node, tapering from 100 mm at the foot to 35 mm at the top, printed as 32 segments about 209 mm tall on an Adventurer 5M. The outside is a plain cone apart from the screw heads. The wall thickens from 3.5 mm at the foot to 4 mm at the top, and is a honeycomb whose ribs the lib sizes to the wind: it works out the bending along the mast for a design gust, the payload's wind area and the two guy points, and widens each segment's ribs until the printed wall stays under the allowable stress, going solid where a segment needs more. Each guy point is a solid band with three pairs of cord holes, and the top 150 mm is solid for the payload's hose clamps. At each joint two solid rings overlap by one hexagon: the upper segment's foot ring over a full-thickness sleeve on the segment below, inside its bore. Push the upper segment down and turn it: a 45° climb draws the foot down onto the joint, a level run keeps it turning, and it pops into its stop with the screw holes in line. M3 cap screws then clamp the foot onto the sleeve.

models.title: Apache Case Modules: MeshCore Repeater
models.description: A modular insert for a Harbor Freight Apache case, first built as a portable MeshCore repeater in an Apache 1800 (small) emptied of its foam. A baseplate fills the case floor with a 20 mm grid of M5 pilots, and every module screws onto the grid with M5 × 10 cap screws, so nothing rattles when the case is carried and any module can move without reprinting the plate. The repeater's modules: a cell bed, in which a 32140 LiFePO4 cell lies front to back against the right end wall, about 1 mm off it. The bed is open on the wall side, so the wall stops the cell rolling out, and two hooks screwed onto its inner post curl over the cell to just past its top and press it down. The cell's charge board sits in a slot across the bed's middle, under the cell, its USB-C and USB-A facing the middle of the case, held by a zip tie. The second module is a tray for the radio's carrier, a 50 × 70 mm perfboard holding an Ebyte E22P-915M30S (1 W SX1262 radio), a Seeed XIAO nRF54LM20A running MeshCore, and a Pololu 5 V boost for the radio. The tray is a pocket with a rim on three sides (the open side for the connectors) and two zip-tie slots that run under it; the board rests on a ledge over a relief for its solder tails. The antenna's N female bulkhead goes through a hole drilled in the case's left end wall, 45 mm above the floor, beside the radio's tray. The case is measured: 214 × 150 inside, 76 deep in the base, an 18 mm lid, r 5 corners; the plate is 212 × 148. The charge board is 33 wide (measured), its length and height estimated. All PETG, printed flat; the hooks print on their sides. Not yet printed.

models.description: Holds the bulkhead jack at the end of an antenna extension cable facing up on a pack's MOLLE, so the antenna stands on top of it. A rounded shroud runs the length of a plate that bolts to Kanix MOLLE clips: seen from above, a half circle round the antenna, squared back to the plate, with a big rounded flange where they meet. The jack goes through the shroud's closed top, its nut on top; its body and the cable run down inside, out a hole at the bottom, so the cable's end is covered. Cable ties through pairs of slots hold the cable down inside: at the bottom end and halfway on the 1×2 and the N, three on the 1×3. The SMA mount is one bolt column, 1×2 or 1×3, 26.4 mm wide like the clip, and pockets the jack's hex so it can't turn. The N mount is a 3×2 bolt pattern on two 1×4 MOLLE clips one PALS channel (38.1 mm) apart, 64.5 mm wide, or on a 3×2 Kanix belt clip; its shroud is bigger and thicker. Bore, walls, flange and cable sizes are customizable. M5×10 screws, PCTG, every edge rounded, no supports. Connector sizes are from other gallery models, not measured on these cables. models.title: E-ink Dual-LoRa Handheld
models.description: A handheld case in the Meshnology N37's shape: a rounded body with a wing at the top left and an antenna bump at the top right, the N37's angled band round its front and back faces, and every edge rounded. A 2.13" e-paper HAT stands portrait down the left of the front. The body runs on down into a full-depth bay for two 18650 cells lying across it, one above the other, 75 × 133 × 26.3 mm (167 mm tall with the wing). Two sealed box switches sit behind the display and press through waterproof two-material buttons in the left side: a TPU boot squeezed against a seal bead on the wall's inside, with a PETG plunger fused into its roof. In the right column, a front-facing XIAO Sense (its microphone through a port, pin holes over its program and reset buttons) sits above a PMW3610 optical sensor board that reads finger swipes through a sealed clear window, where the N37 has its joystick. Two smaller sealed buttons sit right of the window on tact switches the sensor board holds forward, and a front-facing speaker fills the corner below behind a grille, with its I2C amp behind it. The wing holds the L76K's GPS patch facing the front and a strong vibration motor (Precision Microdrives 312-107) behind it; the L76K board sits behind the display. Two SX1262 radios each have their own SMA. The front cover closes onto a tub that holds everything, with six M3 screws from the back. The GPS antenna's size and the swipe sensor's lens footprint are estimates. Not yet printed.

models.title: Solar LoRa Node
models.description: A slim sealed box under a 240 × 168 mm solar panel salvaged from a solar LED lamp, that winches itself up on two cables. The panel drops into a pocket in the frame onto a bead of construction adhesive; a bezel screwed over its border squeezes the bead to 1 mm and leaves the panel flush. The frame and bezel come off the tray as one, on a ring of 24 M3 cap screws outside a TPU gasket that the tray's tongue squeezes from the sides. At the top end, the 10 Ah LP1260110 LiPo pouch lies across the box, centred, under a carrier plate holding the Heltec V3, a TP4056 charger and a 5 V buck-boost; at the bottom end lies a Heltec HT-HC33. An N bulkhead and an SMA bulkhead stand out of opposite ends on the centre line. Under the tray, a deck carries two thin 162 mm spools of 1/32" stainless cable, 100 ft each with room to spare, stacked on one axis at the centre, each on its own 608 skateboard bearing. Each is driven at 8.8:1 by a pinion on the teeth round its edge, from its own JGY-370 worm gearmotor inside the box whose shaft comes down through a TPU lip seal; each pinion sits just outside the other spool's teeth. The cables wind on opposite hands, so the spools turn opposite ways to reel in. 263 × 191 × 67 mm, so it needs a 270 mm bed. The panel's thickness, the buck-boost's size and the motor's dimensions are guesses. Not yet printed.

models.description: A box that rides in a backpack side pouch, carrying a power bank, a Franklin T9 hotspot and three boards: a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, a Heltec HT-HC33 (ESP32-S3 + Wi-Fi HaLow) and a Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V4. The bank lies along the left side behind a full-height divider, held at both ends, its ports toward an open bay at the top end where the cables gather. The T9 lies face up at the bottom of the right side; a cage plate screwed over its port end carries an M3 set screw that holds its power button down, so it always starts. Beside the bank, past the T9, the three boards stand on edge in slots: a groove in the floor between a full-height post at the top end and a low one under each board's USB-C. Two SMA bulkheads through the top wall take the HaLow and LoRa antennas. The lid closes on 21 M3 cap screws, and a tongue round the walls and along the divider drops into a groove under it. 140 × 190 × 47.5 mm with 5 mm walls; the bank's 36.5 mm sets the height. Not yet printed.

models.title: HT-HC33 LiPo Case
models.description: A two-piece case that stands on end, holding a Heltec HT-HC33 (ESP32-S3 + Wi-Fi HaLow), a Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V4, a 103665 LiPo pouch and a USB-C TP4056 charger board, with two SMA bulkheads through its top end and all three USB-Cs out of its bottom. In the base, the cell and the V4 lie flat side by side against the back, a divider between them, the V4 between corner brackets. The HC33 hangs face-in from the lid on four M2 posts over the cell; the TP4056 hangs upside down from the lid over the V4's lower end, on a pad between corner brackets. Two ribs either side of the cell stop just over it and hold it down. The SMAs sit over the V4's column, past the TP4056. Four M3 cap screws go down through corner towers; a tongue round the base's rim drops into a groove under the lid's. 79 × 80 × 27.1 mm (the body 70 × 71). Cell, V4 and TP4056 details are nominal, not measured. Not yet printed.
